::: {.callout-note}
## Relationship to other AffineDrift material

This workspace overlaps with [The Geometry of Motion](../The_Geometry_of_Motion/quarto/index.html), especially Volume I. The difference is editorial rather than doctrinal:

- **Tangent Hyperplane Contraction** is a web-first chapter workspace organized for concise reading, implementation notes, and checklists.
- **The Geometry of Motion** is the broader multi-volume series that carries more of the surrounding mathematical and cross-domain context.

Neither should be treated as a final reference yet. Both remain in development, and overlap between them is intentional.
:::

## Purpose

This workspace organizes a textbook-scale treatment of nonlinear control around tangent-space dynamics, local error evolution, and stability-oriented reasoning in high-dimensional systems. Its role on the site is to move from article-style notes toward a more coherent chapter sequence.

## Plain-Language Summary

At a practical level, the project asks how to make complex motion both effective and repeatable. The proposed answer is to study how small deviations evolve, design feedback using those local dynamics, and check whether the resulting behavior remains well conditioned under the assumptions of the model.

This workspace should be read as an in-development manuscript rather than a settled textbook. Some chapters are closer to polished exposition than others, and the surrounding critique pages remain important context for interpreting the stronger claims.
